question: Should OpenClaw expose these two versioned batch-manifest commands as supported public Memory Wiki CLI contracts, including the accompanying no-op ingest compilation behavior?
rationale: The patch is additive but establishes long-lived automation interfaces and changes an existing operational behavior; correctness checks alone cannot determine whether this product surface belongs in the bundled plugin.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded CLI contract
options.body: Accept the batch commands as supported plugin behavior after redacted real-run proof and explicit review of the existing-vault no-op compilation semantics.

options.title: Narrow to an internal refactor
options.body: Keep reusable batch primitives private and defer public command documentation until the automation contract has an owner-approved design.

options.title: Route the workflow externally
options.body: Decline bundled CLI expansion and pursue an external automation/plugin path only if the current plugin seams can safely support it.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded CLI contract
recommendation.body: Accept the batch commands as supported plugin behavior after redacted real-run proof and explicit review of the existing-vault no-op compilation semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: No reliable current-main Memory Wiki ownership history was available in the supplied review evidence.
